label: Finite causal history and per se regress
term: finite causal history and per se regress
resolution: FiniteDistinctAncestry counts distinct upstream relata via nonempty finite paths in a supplied cause relation. NoCausalLoops excludes revisiting a relatum and is independent of that count: a finite self-loop is the omission model. Accessibility forbids infinite descending histories, including repetitions, but allows infinitely many independent immediate causes. PerSeLinksIncluded is the explicit same-carrier restriction to Aquinas’s per se efficient-cause link. There is no automatic identity between causal-power events in Koons and efficient causes as beings in Aquinas. A broadly quantified finitism covering accidental series would exclude infinite accidental ancestry, whereas Aquinas I q.46 a.2 ad 7 does not regard such regress as impossible; neither reading is rewritten to identify the two. No possible-world quantifier or temporal length bound is formalized; the new premises are unattributed open hypotheses. See docs/notes/causal-finitism-367.md. Owner-approved response-scope forks are now explicit in specs/per-accidens-responses.toml and TruthCore/Causality/PerAccidensResponses.lean: four separate analyst definition/statement siblings distinguish retained capacity from actual exercise, and every from some admissible removal. They are not aliases for the original accidental-series sense and are not conjoined as its definition. The original sense remains unbound and allowlisted pending a faithful identity/applicability mapping; no completed-allowance count is claimed. Actual exercise projects to capacity via the explicit execution-state certificate; universal-to-existential transfer retains admissible-domain nonemptiness. Arbitrary preordered time admits the integer no-first-history control for both generation and successive instruments. The remaining MovesAsMoved and accessibility bridges stay open.
